door-installation-princeton: Doors in Princeton's older houses have often been settling for decades, so a new door has to be fitted to the opening that exists, not the one on the label. Nearly a quarter of the town's homes were built in 1939 or earlier, per the Census Bureau's American Community Survey. We plane, shim, and tune interior and exterior doors from the Western Section to the streets around Nassau Street, replace worn slabs in the same opening, and add deadbolts and keypad locks while the tools are out.
door-installation-west-windsor: Most West Windsor houses went up between the late 1970s and the 2000s, and the builder-grade interior doors in them are now decades past new. We swap them in the same opening, fit new entry and storm doors so there is no daylight around the frame, and get closet doors back on their tracks, all in one trip, from Princeton Junction to Dutch Neck.
door-installation-plainsboro: Plainsboro townhomes in Princeton Collection, Ravens Crest, and Hunters Glen run on bifold closets, sliding patio doors, and hollow-core bedroom doors that have seen a few owners. We re-track, replace, and adjust them inside the unit, and fit a new entry door or storm door where the association allows it.
door-installation-lawrence-township: Lawrence gives us both ends of the door trade: about half the township's homes were built before 1980, where an older frame needs a door fitted rather than just hung, and the rest are newer, where a prehung swap is the quick answer. Either way we finish with weatherstripping that seals and hardware that turns with two fingers, from Lawrenceville to Eldridge Park and Slackwood.
door-installation-montgomery: Entry doors on Montgomery's open lots in Skillman and Belle Mead take wind and weather with nothing to block them, so seals, sweeps, and thresholds matter more here than in a townhome. We install and adjust entry, storm, and interior doors across the township and match the heavier millwork in the newer custom homes.
door-installation-pennington: Pennington Borough doors are mostly old, wood, and worth keeping, so we start by asking whether the door needs replacing or just tuning. We plane and rehang the originals along Main Street where they are sound, replace them in the same opening where they are not, and handle the standard swaps in Brookside and the Hopewell Township streets nearby.
door-installation-south-brunswick: Kendall Park's 1950s and 60s ranches and splits still have a lot of their original interior doors, and many are painted shut or hanging on stripped hinges. We replace and adjust doors across South Brunswick, from those older streets to the newer subdivisions in Dayton and Monmouth Junction, with proper shimming and hardware that works from day one.
door-installation-cranbury: Cranbury's village houses on Main Street and Maplewood Avenue have doors that were hung by hand generations ago, and they deserve to be tuned by hand rather than swapped for a big-box slab. We adjust and repair the originals, and on the newer properties out Cranbury Neck and Old Trenton Road we install entry, storm, and interior doors the standard way.
door-installation-east-windsor: With 60% of East Windsor's homes built before 1980, plenty of doors in Twin Rivers and around Hightstown are on their original hardware or worse: closet doors off the track, bedroom doors that rub, entry doors that leak air. We handle the whole list in one visit, replacing slabs and storm doors in the same opening where the old ones are done.
door-installation-robbinsville: Robbinsville's houses are young by Mercer County standards, so door work is mostly builder hardware wearing out rather than frames gone out of square. We swap knobs, deadbolts, and keypad locks, re-track closet doors in Town Center townhouses and condominiums, and replace entry doors in the same opening.
drywall-repair-princeton: In a town where the median house was built in 1965, a wall repair often means matching what earlier repairs left behind. We patch holes and cracks from the Western Section to the streets off Nassau, feather the edges wide, match the texture, and prime everything so the repair does not flash through the paint.
drywall-repair-west-windsor: Houses from West Windsor's late-1970s-to-2000s building boom tend to crack in the same places: the corners above windows and doors, and along the seams in tall ceilings. We tape those with mesh and setting compound so they stay closed, patch doorknob holes and anchor damage, and replace water-stained board after the leak is fixed, from Princeton Junction to Grovers Mill.
drywall-repair-plainsboro: Townhome drywall in Plainsboro has usually been patched a few times by previous owners, and not always well. We cut out the bad work in Princeton Collection, Ravens Crest, and Fox Run units, tape and feather properly, match the texture, and leave it primed. Water stains on a ceiling get a straight answer about where the water came from.
drywall-repair-lawrence-township: Lawrence Township's housing runs from pre-1980 homes in Lawrenceville to newer houses along Princeton Pike, and wall damage looks different in each. We repair each with the right materials, feathering patches wide and matching texture so the fix disappears once it is painted.
drywall-repair-montgomery: Montgomery's newer homes in Skillman and Belle Mead have tall ceilings and long unbroken walls where a patch has nowhere to hide, so we feather wide and prime before paint. Nail pops, settling cracks, and damage from a moved TV mount are the usual calls, along with ceiling repairs after a bathroom or roof leak has been fixed.
drywall-repair-pennington: Pennington Borough walls along Main Street are often plaster over lath, which cracks differently and needs a different repair than drywall. We patch plaster properly, repair drywall in the Brookside and Hopewell Township streets, and match textures so the repair is not visible under paint.
drywall-repair-south-brunswick: Kendall Park's older ranches and splits have drywall that has been through sixty years of hanging pictures and a few remodels, while Dayton and Monmouth Junction homes crack along the window corners and ceiling seams as they settle. We repair both across South Brunswick and prime every patch so it does not flash.
drywall-repair-cranbury: Cranbury's historic village houses are plaster and horsehair in places, and we treat them accordingly: no drywall screws into old lath, no quick-set over a crack that needs to be keyed in. Newer homes toward Cranbury Neck get standard drywall patching, texture matching, and priming.
drywall-repair-east-windsor: Many East Windsor homes, Twin Rivers included, have decades of drywall repairs in them, some good and some not. We cut out the failed patches, retape, and blend so the wall reads as one surface. Water-damaged board comes out rather than getting painted over.
drywall-repair-robbinsville: Robbinsville drywall is newer, which means the damage is mostly life, not age: doorknob holes, anchors pulled out by a fallen shelf, cracks at the corners as the house finishes settling. We patch, texture, and prime across Town Center, New Sharon, and the rest of the township, and most lists fit inside one $345 visit.
deck-staining-princeton: A shaded Princeton deck sees more mildew and moss than sun fade. We wash thoroughly, let the wood dry, replace the soft boards, and stain during a dry stretch. On older houses near Nassau Street and in the Western Section we treat wood porches the same way, with finishes that suit the age of the house.
deck-staining-west-windsor: Many West Windsor decks were built along with the houses and have gone too long between coats. We wash, sand the rough spots, swap any punky boards, tighten the railings, and stain on a dry weather window across Princeton Junction, Dutch Neck, and Grovers Mill. Every two to three years and the deck outlives the mortgage.
deck-staining-plainsboro: Plainsboro's single-family homes have decks that need the standard restore: wash, dry, repair, stain. In the townhome communities the association usually owns the exterior, so ask your HOA first; where decks belong to the unit, we treat them like any other deck and schedule around the forecast, not the calendar.
deck-staining-lawrence-township: Decks on Lawrence Township's newer houses are hitting the age where the sealer is long gone and the boards are graying. We bring them back with a proper wash, board replacement where needed, and stain applied to dry wood. Older porches in Lawrenceville get the same care with finishes suited to the house.
deck-staining-montgomery: Montgomery's large-lot decks in Skillman and Belle Mead get full sun and full wind, so they weather faster than a shaded townhome deck. We wash, replace the boards that have split, tighten the rails, and stain with a product suited to the exposure. Bigger decks and pool decks get one written price for the whole job.
deck-staining-pennington: Pennington decks and porches, from Brookside back yards to Main Street porches, get the same sequence: wash, dry, repair, stain. We schedule around a dry stretch of weather because stain on damp wood fails early, and we replace the soft boards first so the finish is not just painting over a problem.
deck-staining-south-brunswick: South Brunswick decks in Dayton and Monmouth Junction are twenty to thirty years old and often on their first restain ever. We wash off the gray, sand, replace cracked boards, tighten railings, and stain across the township, including the older Kendall Park decks that need a few more boards than most.
deck-staining-cranbury: Cranbury decks range from small village back yards to larger decks on the Cranbury Neck properties. We prep properly, replace what is soft, and stain with the right product for the wood and the exposure.
deck-staining-east-windsor: Decks on East Windsor's single-family streets are due, and many of the older ones need boards and a railing fix before stain goes on. We fold repair, wash, and stain into one job with one written price. Twin Rivers exterior work belongs to the association in most cases, so check there first.
deck-staining-robbinsville: Robbinsville decks are newer but were often left bare since the day the builder finished, so the first coat of stain is overdue. We wash, sand, and stain across New Sharon, Windsor, and the rest of the township, with a repair-versus-replace opinion on any boards that have cupped or split.
fence-repair-princeton: Princeton fences lean, sag, and rot like everyone else's, and on the older properties some picket and split-rail fences need parts made rather than bought. We reset posts, replace pickets and panels, and rehang gates across town, matching what is there rather than selling you a new fence.
fence-repair-west-windsor: West Windsor's privacy and picket fences mostly went in with the houses, and the posts are the weak point after decades of freeze-thaw. We dig out and reset leaning posts in concrete, replace the rotted ones, swap panels, and rehang gates so they latch, from Princeton Junction to Penns Neck.
fence-repair-plainsboro: Fence repair for Plainsboro's single-family homes: posts reset, panels and pickets replaced, gates fixed so they close. In the townhome communities fences are usually the association's responsibility, so check with your HOA; where they are yours, we repair rather than replace and match the existing style.
fence-repair-lawrence-township: Lawrence Township fences run from chain-link and wood on older lots in Eldridge Park and Slackwood to privacy fence on newer ones. We reset leaning posts, replace broken pickets and rails, fix chain-link, and rebuild gates so they swing and latch cleanly.
fence-repair-montgomery: Montgomery's open lots take wind that a townhome fence never sees, and a stretch of privacy fence in Skillman or Belle Mead can go over in a single storm. We reset and replace posts, rebuild damaged sections, and rehang gates with hardware that will not rust out in two seasons. Split-rail and paddock fence repairs too.
fence-repair-pennington: Pennington fence work runs from picket repairs on Main Street, where style has to fit the house, to standard wood and vinyl fence repairs in Brookside and the surrounding Hopewell Township streets. Gate sag, post rot, and broken panels are the usual calls, and we match the existing fence so the repair does not advertise itself.
fence-repair-south-brunswick: South Brunswick fences in Kendall Park are often more patch than fence by now, and the newer privacy fences in Dayton and Monmouth Junction are failing at the posts. We tell you honestly what is worth saving, reset or replace the posts, swap panels and pickets, and rehang gates with latches that catch.
fence-repair-cranbury: Cranbury fence repair covers the village's picket and split-rail fences, which need parts that suit the period, and the wood and vinyl fences on the newer properties toward Cranbury Neck. Post resets, panel swaps, and gate rebuilds are the bread and butter, with a straight opinion when a section is past saving.
fence-repair-east-windsor: Fences on East Windsor's single-family streets take the same beating as everyone's: heaved posts, rotted bottoms, gates that drag. We reset posts, replace boards and panels, and rehang gates. In Twin Rivers the association handles most fencing, so ask them before booking.
fence-repair-robbinsville: Robbinsville fences are newer, so the repairs are usually storm damage and gate hardware rather than rot: a panel blown out, a gate that sags because the hinges were never right. We fix what broke, brace the gate, and match the existing fence across New Sharon, Windsor, and the rest of the township.
